R661.note: Correct JNDI parameterized search({0},{1}) replacing concatenation; matches original 4-arg search() overload.

R662.note: Would not compile: ExecuteSqlRawAsync has no FormattableString overload (that's ExecuteSqlInterpolatedAsync/ExecuteSqlAsync); passing a FormattableString-typed local to ExecuteSqlRawAsync(string,...) is a CS1503 type error.

R663.note: Removes the double-decode and adds toRealPath()+startsWith() containment check; matches original servlet structure.

R664.note: Extension allowlist plus UUID-based filename closes both dangerous-type and traversal risk cleanly.

R665.note: Removes the /e eval but replaces it with call_user_func($formatter, $vars[$key]) where $formatter is still taken straight from $_POST with no validation - the case comment explicitly notes a formatter value of 'system' runs arbitrary code, and that capability is unchanged, only relocated. Whitelist validation is mentioned as 'additional hardening' but not implemented, so the residual gap is at least disclosed.

R666.note: Extension allowlist blocks dangerous types but destPath still joins avatarDir with the raw, unsanitized header.Filename, so a name like '../../x.png' still escapes avatarDir for an arbitrary-path write; the write-up only mentions randomizing the filename as an optional 'consider' rather than applying it.

R667.note: Swapping BinaryFormatter for System.Text.Json with a concrete type correctly blocks gadget-chain RCE, but it silently changes the wire format - any existing binary-serialized session blobs will fail to deserialize; this is only weakly flagged via an optional DataContractSerializer alternative rather than called out as a required migration.

R668.note: Upload-side fix (extension allowlist + random filename) is solid, but avatar_lookup.go's ReadAvatarBytes(originalFilename) is never updated and no new filename is returned to the caller, so every previously-working retrieval silently breaks - directly violating the stated contract, and not mentioned in the write-up at all.

R669.note: fgets() closes the stack overflow, but the fix only checks len against out_capacity, not against line's own 64-byte capacity, and never detects/drains a line fgets truncated (missing trailing '\n'). A too-long line is silently accepted (truncated) rather than rejected, and leftover bytes remain in stdin to corrupt the next read - exactly what the stated contract requires to be prevented.

R670.note: Removing @csrf_exempt restores Django's default CSRF middleware check; rest of the view (401/405 JSON shapes, queue_change call) is untouched, matching the contract.

R671.note: ArgumentList plus a strict alphanumeric allowlist for reportName; the write-up itself is honest that .bat re-invocation can still let cmd.exe reparse, and the allowlist neutralizes any metacharacters regardless.

R672.note: Decoding into a narrow AccountRequest DTO and building Account server-side blocks the IsAdmin/Balance mass-assignment; added empty-username rejection and MaxBytesReader are minor, clearly disclosed hardening.

R673.note: Swapping wtforms.Form for FlaskForm is sufficient on its own (Flask-WTF's validate() checks CSRF regardless of validate_on_submit()), correctly requires no handler changes; template/csrf_token guidance is accurate.

R674.note: Logs the clientId parameter (already stored, identical value) instead of the freed req->clientId; matches the documented ownership contract exactly.

R675.note: Adds secure=True alongside existing httponly=True; minimal, correct, no behavior change for legitimate HTTPS use.

R676.note: Replaces the file-reading lookupRate with an allowlisted rate dictionary while leaving Eval() itself intact for arithmetic - matches the stated contract precisely.

R677.note: Moves validation to post-write magic-byte detection via file-type, discards the client-supplied mimetype/extension entirely, and cleans up rejected files; sound and matches multer's diskStorage/fileFilter API.

R678.note:
th:text closes the XSS but fully escapes bodyHtml, so the intentionally rendered '

Draft body

' now displays as literal tag text instead of formatted content - the contract calls for allowlist-sanitized rich text to keep rendering, and that's only offered as an optional aside ('if the application genuinely requires...'), not the shipped fix.

R679.note: Wraps exportUsersHandler with the existing requireAdmin middleware exactly as banUserHandler/unbanUserHandler already are; precise match to the case.

R680.note: Adds bcrypt.compare() against a stored hash before authenticating; field-name assumption (passwordHash) is explicitly disclosed.

R681.note: HttpGet->HttpPost plus ValidateAntiForgeryToken is correct, but it necessarily breaks the existing GET-based 'delete' link/flow; the write-up does openly state the confirmation page must be changed to POST with an antiforgery token, so this is a disclosed required follow-up rather than a silent break.

R682.note: Runs ping.exe directly with discrete args, bypassing cmd.exe/shell entirely; correct and preserves the diagnostic output behavior.

R683.note: WHERE id = ANY($1) with the ids array as a parameter is idiomatic node-postgres and preserves selecting exactly the given ids, matching the contract.

R684.note: Re-indexes tasks[activeIndex] instead of reusing the reference invalidated by push_back; correct and preserves intended semantics.

R685.note: doc.XmlResolver = null before LoadXml() is the standard, minimal fix for this exact XmlDocument XXE pattern; no other behavior changed.

R686.note: Same case/fix as R661 - correct parameterized JNDI search.

R687.note: Parameterized query with ? placeholder is correct for database/sql; note the explanation's claim that the driver auto-translates ? to $1 for Postgres is not accurate (placeholder syntax is driver-specific, not translated by database/sql), though the case doesn't reveal which driver is in use.

R688.note: Captures bytesSent() before the reset() that destroys the original Resource; returned value is identical to what the original code intended to return.

R689.note: Same toRealPath()+startsWith() containment pattern as R663, correctly applied to this OWASP Benchmark case.

R690.note: unserialize($payload, ['allowed_classes' => false]) blocks object instantiation/gadget chains while preserving the existing wire format and array shape for legitimate carts; matches this codebase's own documented CWE-502 doctrine for PHP.

R691.note: enable_shared_from_this + capturing a shared_ptr instead of raw this correctly extends Widget's lifetime to cover the queued callback; full rewrite is internally consistent.

R692.note: Standard @ownerName parameterized SqlCommand fix, correct and behavior-preserving.

R693.note: pool.execute() with a ? placeholder and userId as a bound parameter is correct mysql2 usage, same callback shape as before.

R694.note: HTML::Entities::encode_entities() applied to both attacker-controlled fields only, leaving the trusted status badge markup untouched.

R695.note: Parameterized search({0}, filterArgs, SearchControls) with default SearchControls correctly reproduces the original search(name, filter, null) default-controls behavior while escaping data.

R696.note: jwt.verify() with an explicit algorithms allowlist replaces the unverified jwt.decode(); standard, correct fix.

R697.note: Passes null for the exec() environment array, removing the sole attacker-controlled input from the vulnerable overload entirely; command args were never user-controlled to begin with.

R698.note: Swapping to xml2js (sax-based, no DTD support) correctly closes XXE, but the extraction doc?.order?.[0]?.id?.[0] is wrong: xml2js's default explicitRoot does not array-wrap the root element, so doc.order is an object, not an array, and this indexing returns undefined for every legitimate input - the endpoint would always report 'missing order id', silently and undisclosed.

R699.note: Moves the priority assignment before push_back so it uses the still-valid reference; final state (both current and follow-up priority set to completionPriority) is unchanged from the original intent.

R700.note: Type-asserts token.Method as *jwt.SigningMethodHMAC inside keyFunc plus jwt.WithValidMethods([]string{"HS256"}); both are real golang-jwt/v5 APIs and correctly block algorithm-confusion.
